title: Forces and Equilibrium Module 1 Lesson 3: Constrained Resultants custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: Two forces act on a particle: a force of $24\text{ N}$ acting along the positive $x$-axis and a force of magnitude $F$ acting at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the negative $x$-axis. Given that the resultant of the two forces acts purely in the vertical direction (along the positive $y$-axis), calculate the value of $F$, and find the magnitude of the resultant force.

Two forces act at a point $O$: a force of $40\text{ N}$ along the positive $y$-axis and a force of $50\text{ N}$ acting at an acute angle $\alpha$ below the positive $x$-axis. Given that the resultant force acts purely in the horizontal direction (along the positive $x$-axis), calculate the angle $\alpha$, and find the magnitude of the resultant force.

Three coplanar forces act at a point: a force of $35\text{ N}$ along the positive $x$-axis, a force of $20\text{ N}$ at an angle of $60^\circ$ above the positive $x$-axis, and a vertical force $P$ acting in the negative $y$-direction. Given that the resultant of the three forces acts entirely along the positive $x$-axis, determine the value of $P$, and state the magnitude of the resultant force.

Two forces act at a point $O$: a force of $18\text{ N}$ in the positive $x$-direction and a force $Q$ in the positive $y$-direction. The resultant force $\mathbf{R}$ acts along a line inclined at an angle of $45^\circ$ to the positive $x$-axis. Calculate the value of $Q$, and determine the magnitude of the resultant force $\mathbf{R}$.

A force of magnitude $25\text{ N}$ acts at an angle $\alpha$ above the positive $x$-axis, where $\cos\alpha = 0.8$ and $\sin\alpha = 0.6$. A second force of magnitude $P$ acts at an angle $\beta$ below the positive $x$-axis. The resultant of the two forces has magnitude $40\text{ N}$ and acts purely along the positive $x$-axis. Calculate the values of $P\sin\beta$ and $P\cos\beta$, and hence determine the value of $P$.

A force $\mathbf{P}$ of magnitude $30\text{ N}$ acts along the positive $x$-axis. A second force $\mathbf{Q}$ is applied such that the resultant force $\mathbf{R}$ has magnitude $40\text{ N}$ and acts along the positive $y$-axis. Calculate the magnitude of $\mathbf{Q}$, and find the angle that $\mathbf{Q}$ makes with the negative $x$-axis, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

questions.prompt:
Three coplanar forces act at a point $O$:
- A force of magnitude $28\text{ N}$ acts along the positive $x$-axis.
- A force of magnitude $30\text{ N}$ acts at an angle $\alpha$ above the positive $x$-axis, where $\cos\alpha = 0.8$ and $\sin\alpha = 0.6$.
- A force of magnitude $P$ acts at an angle of $30^\circ$ below the negative $x$-axis.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Write down expressions in terms of $P$ for the total component $X$ in the positive $x$-direction and the total component $Y$ in the positive $y$-direction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that the resultant of the three forces acts entirely along the positive $x$-axis (so that $Y = 0$), find the value of $P$, and calculate the magnitude of the resultant force, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt:
Three coplanar forces act at a point $O$:
- A force of magnitude $40\text{ N}$ acts along the positive $x$-axis.
- A force of magnitude $50\text{ N}$ acts at an angle $\theta$ above the negative $x$-axis, where $\cos\theta = 0.6$ and $\sin\theta = 0.8$.
- A force of magnitude $F$ acts along the negative $y$-axis.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total component $X$ of the resultant force in the $x$-direction, and deduce that $X$ is independent of the value of $F$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that the resultant force acts at an angle of $45^\circ$ below the positive $x$-axis, determine the value of $F$, and calculate the magnitude of the resultant force.

questions.prompt:
Four coplanar forces act at a point $O$:
- A force of $65\text{ N}$ acts at an angle $\alpha$ in the first quadrant, where $\cos\alpha = \frac{12}{13}$ and $\sin\alpha = \frac{5}{13}$.
- A force of $20\text{ N}$ acts along the positive $y$-axis.
- A force of $P\text{ N}$ acts at an angle $\theta$ above the negative $x$-axis (where $0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$).
- A force of $15\text{ N}$ acts along the negative $y$-axis.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Given that the resultant of the four forces is zero in the vertical direction (so that the resultant is entirely horizontal) and that $P = 50\text{ N}$, find the value of $\theta$, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using the value of $\theta$ found in part (a), calculate the magnitude and direction of the resultant force.

questions.prompt:
Three coplanar forces act at a point $O$:
- A force of magnitude $P$ acting at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the positive $x$-axis.
- A force of magnitude $Q$ acting at an angle of $60^\circ$ above the negative $x$-axis.
- A downward vertical force of magnitude $30\text{ N}$ acting along the negative $y$-axis.
The resultant force $\mathbf{R}$ has a magnitude of $20\text{ N}$ and acts entirely along the positive $x$-axis (so that $R_x = 20\text{ N}$ and $R_y = 0$).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
By resolving the forces horizontally and vertically, show that:
$$P\sqrt{3} - Q = 40$$
and find a second linear equation connecting $P$ and $Q$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Solve these simultaneous equations to find the exact values of $P$ and $Q$ in surd form, and give each value correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt:
Three coplanar forces of magnitudes $25\text{ N}$, $40\text{ N}$, and $F\text{ N}$ act at a point $O$:
- The $25\text{ N}$ force acts along the positive $x$-axis.
- The $40\text{ N}$ force acts at an angle of $60^\circ$ above the positive $x$-axis.
- The force $F$ acts along the positive $y$-axis.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Write down simplified expressions in terms of $F$ for the horizontal component $X$ and the vertical component $Y$ of the resultant force.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that the resultant force $\mathbf{R}$ makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the positive $x$-axis (so that $\tan 60^\circ = \frac{Y}{X}$), calculate the exact value of $F$, and express your answer in the form $a\sqrt{3}$ where $a$ is an integer.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force $\mathbf{R}$ in this case.

questions.prompt:
A particle of mass $m = 5\text{ kg}$ is at rest on a smooth horizontal floor. Three horizontal forces act on the particle:
- $\mathbf{F}_1$ of magnitude $48\text{ N}$ acting along the positive $x$-axis.
- $\mathbf{F}_2$ of magnitude $49\text{ N}$ acting along the positive $y$-axis.
- $\mathbf{F}_3$ of unknown magnitude $P$ acting at an angle $\alpha$ below the negative $x$-axis (where $0^\circ < \alpha < 90^\circ$).
The resultant force $\mathbf{R}$ acts entirely in the positive $y$-direction and has magnitude $35\text{ N}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving along the coordinate axes, determine the value of $\alpha$ and the value of $P$, giving $\alpha$ correct to 1 decimal place and $P$ correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt:
Given that the particle is released from rest at $t = 0$ under the action of this resultant force:
(i) calculate the acceleration of the particle,
(ii) determine the speed of the particle and the distance it has travelled after $4\text{ seconds}$.

questions.prompt:
Three coplanar forces act at a point $O$:
- A force of magnitude $60\text{ N}$ along the positive $x$-axis.
- A force of magnitude $45\text{ N}$ along the positive $y$-axis.
- A force of magnitude $P$ acting at an angle $\theta$ to the positive $x$-axis (measured anticlockwise, where $0^\circ \leqslant \theta \leqslant 360^\circ$).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Given that the resultant of the three forces is perpendicular to the $60\text{ N}$ force (so that the resultant acts purely along the $y$-axis):
(i) show that $P\cos\theta = -60$,
(ii) state the minimum possible value of the force magnitude $P$, and find the corresponding value of $\theta$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For the case where $P$ has this minimum value of $60\text{ N}$ and $\theta = 180^\circ$, determine the magnitude and direction of the resultant force.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt:
Suppose instead that $P = 75\text{ N}$, and the angle $\theta$ is chosen such that the resultant force acts along the line $y = x$ (at an angle of $45^\circ$ to the positive $x$-axis, so that $Y = X$).
(i) Show that $\sin\theta - \cos\theta = 0.2$.
(ii) Find the two possible values of $\theta$ in the range $0^\circ \leqslant \theta \leqslant 360^\circ$, giving each value correct to 1 decimal place.
